record.context_brief: Real-negative zeros of a 2Psi1 Wright function
record.original_question:
Consider the Wright function 2Ψ1(x) = Σ_{k≥0} Γ(ak+1)Γ(bk+1) x^k /
(Γ(ck+d+1) k!), where a, b, c, d are nonnegative and
c ≥ a+b. Determine additional restrictions on the parameters a, b, c,
and d that guarantee that 2Ψ1(x) has only real
negative zeros.

evidence.quote: Problem 28 ([24], p. 90 in [51]). Consider ∞ X Γ(ak + 1)Γ(bk + 1) xk Ψ (x) = , 2 1 Γ(ck + d + 1) k! a, b, c, d ≥ 0 and c ≥ a + b.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the Wright-type function
$$\,_2\Psi_1(x)\;=\;\sum_{k\ge 0}\frac{\Gamma(ak+1)\,\Gamma(bk+1)}{\Gamma(ck+d+1)}\,\frac{x^k}{k!},$$
where $a,b,c,d$ are nonnegative real parameters satisfying $c\ge a+b$ (so that the series converges for all $x\in\mathbb{C}$ and defines an entire function).

Determine additional conditions on the parameters $a,b,c,d\ge 0$ (subject to $c\ge a+b$) under which the entire function $\,_2\Psi_1(x)$ has only real, strictly negative zeros.
artifact.category_tag: Zeros of entire functions / Wright functions
artifact.status_search_result: General results on zeros of the classical one-parameter Wright function are known (e.g. for the function φ(ρ,β;z) with ρ>0 all but finitely many zeros are simple and real negative), but a direct, complete characterization of the parameters (a,b,c,d) for the two-parameter Fox–Wright series $\,_2\Psi_1$ guaranteeing only real negative zeros was not located in the search; the problem appears to remain unresolved in published literature.

status_evidence.title: On the distribution of zeros of the Wright function
status_evidence.snippet: In the case ρ > 0 all zeros with large enough k are simple and are lying on the negative real semi-axis.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic distribution of zeros is understood for the classical Wright function but not for the two-parameter Fox–Wright form considered here.

status_evidence.title: Fox–Wright function - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Fox–Wright generalized hypergeometric function definition and convergence conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The series defines an entire function under c ≥ a+b.
